key_insight: MindForge tackles a major gap in coding agents by training small language models to handle software engineering from scratch, not just edit existing code. It creates a source-free program synthesis setting that spans the whole software lifecycle, enabling broader and more realistic code-generation capabilities.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the difficulty of teaching AI systems to build complete software projects from the ground up. Existing benchmarks and training environments mostly focus on modifying existing code, while from-scratch program construction remains extremely challenging and poorly supported at scale.
method: Introduces a source-free software engineering training setting that does not rely on existing codebases.
Models the whole-life-cycle of software development, covering program creation beyond bug fixing or feature completion.
Uses program synthesis tasks to train small language models in realistic end-to-end coding workflows.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work points to a path for making smaller models useful in real software engineering pipelines, not just narrow code-editing tasks. It may improve training data design, benchmarking, and agent robustness for end-to-end code generation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing the whole software engineering life cycle from requirements to finished program
Comparison chart: code editing tasks vs from-scratch program synthesis
Benchmark/score graphic highlighting the difficulty gap on ProgramBench
Icon set for planning, coding, testing, debugging, and deployment
paper_title: MindForge: Teaching Small Language Models Whole-Life-Cycle Software Engineering via Source-Free Program Synthesis
paper_authors: Yihao Chen, Shi Chang, Khaled Chawa, Feng Lin, Boyuan Chen
